note: Candidate browser mutations of the area tests (final audit after Stage 8), written by its first session and not run: no browser in this phase. Each: the hypothesis, the reproduction in an isolated copy, the expected outcome and why it matters.

candidates.hypothesis: The in-app self-test checks the decided arrow cap against the code's own constant (ARROW_CAP.PX), so changing the decision's value is caught only by css-test.js's source pin, not by the self-test.
candidates.repro: In an isolated copy: app.js:2838 `var ARROW_CAP={PX:16, Q:1.1, OP:0.62, M:0.97}` -> `{PX:24, ...}`; python3 build.py; npm run check:selftest (and node css-test.js).
candidates.expected: css-test.js fails ("ARROW_CAP is not {PX:16, ...}"); the self-test check "arrows (decision 241): ... at most 24 px" passes (its name changes with the constant, so the manifest check fails on the name only).
candidates.why: Shows which layer actually holds an owner-decided value: the self-test verifies behaviour against the code, css-test.js pins the number.

candidates.hypothesis: The self-test's derived-reading check catches a march row without its derived tag (node: runtime-test.js catches it; css-test.js's pin does not, M08).
candidates.repro: app.js:7929: remove `+" "+derivedTag()` from marchRow's last return; build; npm run check:selftest.
candidates.expected: FAIL "derived readings tagged: every formation's march row ..." (derivedTagChecks, app.js:11075).
candidates.why: Confirms the browser layer of decision 125/D-6's labelling, already confirmed in node.

candidates.hypothesis: check:contrast reads computed colours of visible text in its 45 states but no :hover/:focus/:active rule, and css-test.js reads no colour literal in style.css outside the 5G inset (M13): a low-contrast hover colour typed into style.css passes every check.
candidates.repro: style.css: `#sc-clear:hover{color:var(--text)}` -> `#sc-clear:hover{color:#3a3f44}` (about 1.8:1 on --panel #131A21); build; npm run check:contrast; node css-test.js.
candidates.why: Tests the claim that tokens.js is the only source of interface colours and the reach of the contrast check.

candidates.hypothesis: A lowered text token is caught by check:contrast.
candidates.repro: tokens.js theme.dark "text-muted": "#9BA3A9" -> "#5A6268"; python3 build.py --tokens; python3 build.py; npm run check:contrast.
candidates.expected: CONTRAST fails with text below AA in several states.
candidates.why: Positive control for the contrast check (the node suites only check the tokens' copy).

candidates.hypothesis: The harness's figure-on-ground check passes when no figure is measured: requirements() does not demand figures.count>0 in a landscape case (thresholds.js:429-430).
candidates.repro: app.js:1249 kitWrap: delete `(gear?GEAR_ALL:KIT_ALL).push(w);` (the meshes' own geometries no longer listed by kitGeos); build; npm run check:visual -- or harness --only pratzen-low.
candidates.expected: The case's figures.count drops (to the shared geometries' instances only, possibly 0) and "a figure is N units off the drawn ground" is not evaluated; whether some other check fails (the self-test's kit checks, culling) tells how exposed the gap is.
candidates.why: On this build the count is 5,995-6,059 per landscape case (docs/stage8-evidence/8l/report-two-cases.json), so the gap is theoretical unless a refactor breaks the listing.

candidates.hypothesis: Presentation code that overrides a guarded datum at start-up passes the self-test and check:visual as it passes every node check (M29).
candidates.repro: app.js:613 init(): insert `FORMATIONS.sthilaire.track[5].p=[287,295];` as its first statement; build; npm run check:selftest; npm run check:data.
candidates.expected: All pass; check:data lists init among the changed interface declarations and exits 0.
candidates.why: The screen is not held to the declared data by any check; a deep freeze of the guarded declarations before init (in the self-test or runtime-test) would catch it.

candidates.hypothesis: No check reads the formation dossier's strength row against the data (M30).
candidates.repro: app.js:7975: `var str=f.strength||aggStrength(id);` (dossierFormation) -> `var str=Math.round((f.strength||aggStrength(id))*1.25);`; build; npm run check:selftest; npm run check:contrast.
candidates.why: The visitor reads strengths in the dossier; a display error there would be materially misleading.

candidates.hypothesis: The motion block holds the map layer's band: removing it raises jumps and pops over the 248/998 ceilings.
candidates.repro: app.js:5339 MLS `BAND:0.08` -> `BAND:0`; build; npm run check:selftest.
candidates.expected: css-test.js fails on its MLS pin; check:selftest fails on the motion block's totals (jumps/pops over 248/998) or visibility.
candidates.why: Positive control that the benchmark ceilings, pinned at the build's own counts, are live.

candidates.hypothesis: Culling's widening by the animation's envelope is held by the self-test and the cull motion block.
candidates.repro: app.js:1059 animEnv(g): return 0 at its start; build; npm run check:selftest; check:visual's cull block.
candidates.expected: FAIL "culling (8E's prerequisite, the audit of 8D): the bounds follow the geometry drawn and the animation's definition"; possibly pixel differences in the cull block.
candidates.why: The oracle there is animAt (the JS mirror), so this also shows how far the mirror-based checks reach.

candidates.hypothesis: The gait's GLSL and its JavaScript mirror (animAt) can diverge without a failing check except at the few source-pinned lines.
candidates.repro: In animGLSL (app.js near 1865), scale the thigh swing (parts 1, 2) by 1.5 in the GLSL only, leaving animAt unchanged; build; npm run check:selftest; check:contrast's context-gait case.
candidates.expected: Most likely all pass (the contact check (h) and the culling oracle use animAt); a pixel-level check of a posed mesh against animAt would catch it.
candidates.why: Measures the independence of the gait checks from the code under test.

candidates.hypothesis: Wall-clock budgets fail under load without a defect (T-7, inherited): the self-test's pan move (msMove<=2 ms at the median, app.js:11322) and the harness's layer pass (LAYER_MS 8 ms).
candidates.repro: Run npm run check:selftest twice on the unchanged build: once alone, once beside a CPU load of 4 busy processes on 4 cores; compare the pan-move median and the layer pass times.
candidates.expected: Medians rise with load; a failure under load alone would be a flake to record, not a defect.
candidates.why: This audit's own checks ran at load averages of 20-37 on 4 cores.
